# How to read

Under each question there is a `- [ ] A:` line.

- **Tick it without writing anything:** you agree with the proposal.
- **Tick it and add a detail:** you agree, with that detail.
- **Leave it unticked and write:** I revise the proposal.

Nothing here is built. The starting point is the idea in `TODO.md`: register your own
devices in Joma; send them files, clipboard and images, and share or control their
screens; messages reach a contact as long as any of your devices is online; choose what
contacts see of your devices; later, agents among your devices.

# What Jami already does

Read in the daemon's code (`upstream/jami-daemon`), to verify in the test nest:

- **One account, many devices.** A Jami account is one identity; each device linked to it
  (with a PIN or QR code: `addDevice`) gets its own certificate. Contacts see one
  person. `getKnownRingDevices` lists the account's devices; `revokeDevice` removes a
  lost one; each has a name.
- **Conversations live on every device.** A conversation is a git repository copied on
  every member's devices, ours included.
- **Sending already has redundancy.** A message is committed on the device that writes
  it, announced *first to our own other devices*, then to the members
  (`sendMessageNotification`). A peer's device syncs from any member device it reaches.
  The airplane case then already works: the laptop sends, the phone gets the commit, the
  contact comes online later and fetches it from the phone.
  - The gap: none of our other devices was online while the laptop was. The message then
    waits on the laptop.
- **Statuses** per member: sent, delivered, read (`messageStatus`).
- **Presence** is per device on the network; the daemon sums it up per contact (online
  when any device is reachable). Contacts reach our devices directly, so Jami's
  reachability cannot be hidden per device.
- **Notes to self** (a conversation with only us) is synced to all our devices.

# A. The model

**Q1. Devices are devices of one Jami account, not separate accounts tied by Joma.**

- **Proposal:** your devices are linked to the same account, Jami's way. Joma adds what
  Jami lacks: a page of your devices, actions aimed at one device, and per-device
  presence for Joma users.
- **Why:**
  - the redundancy and the sync of history come for free (above);
  - contacts keep seeing one person;
  - the Jami app on the phone keeps working: an Android phone with Jami is just one more
    device.
- **Alternative** (one account per device, linked by Joma under a "user"):
  - contacts would see one contact per device unless every Joma merged them;
  - redundancy, history and read status would have to be rebuilt by Joma;
  - the Jami app would not understand any of it.

- [ ] A:

**Q2. A "your devices" page.**

- **The list:** name, "this device", online or last seen, platform (Joma, Jami app),
  and the device ID (copy).
- **Link a new device:** Jami's PIN or QR code, both directions:
  - this one invites another;
  - a new Joma joins an existing account.
- **Rename** a device; **revoke** a lost one (password asked when the account has one).
- **Where:**
  - in Contacts, a "you" group on top with your devices, each with the same quick
    buttons as a contact (Q3);
  - the full management in the account settings (J7).

- [ ] A:

# B. Doing things with your devices

**Q3. Sending to your devices.**

- **To all of them:** files, images, clipboard and text go to *Notes to self*, which
  every device syncs. This needs no new protocol.
- **To one device:** the same, plus a Joma account message naming the target device
  (`to_device`). Only that one acts:
  - it saves the file;
  - it puts the text or image on its clipboard;
  - it notifies.
- **Clipboard:** a "send clipboard" button and a key (proposal: Ctrl+Shift+V is taken
  by video calls, so Ctrl+Alt+C). The receiving device sets its clipboard
  (`wl-copy` on Omarchy) and says so in a notification. Never set silently: a
  per-device switch, off by default, allows it.

- [ ] A:

**Q4. Screen and remote control between your devices.**

- **The screen:** the desktop share without a call already exists between Joma peers.
  It works between your own devices too, through a Jami service tunnel to *that*
  device. To verify: Jami routes a call to our own account to the other devices.
- **Remote control is new:**
  - the viewer sends pointer and key events over the same tunnel;
  - the shared device injects them through the desktop portal's RemoteDesktop. Hyprland
    supports it through xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland: to verify.
- **Rules:**
  - only between your own devices;
  - the first time on each device it asks, and it remembers per device;
  - a red frame and a banner on the controlled screen;
  - Esc three times, or the banner button, stops it.

- [ ] A:

**Q5. Message delivery: rely on Jami, measure it, add only what is missing.**

- **First,** a test in the nest with three profiles:
  - two are linked devices of one account;
  - the sender goes offline right after sending;
  - the contact comes online later.

  Jami's sync should deliver the message from the second device.
- **Joma adds:**
  - the message status in the chat (sent, delivered, read);
  - a line on the sender's other devices: "waiting for Bob: kept by 2 of your devices".
- **A retry layer of its own** (each device checks every N minutes and resends) only if
  the test shows gaps. Jami's commits are already shared state, so "sent" and
  "delivered" update on every device without Joma marking anything.

- [ ] A:

# C. What contacts see

**Q6. Online, active, and your devices.**

- **Two states for contacts, as now:**
  - *reachable* (Jami: a device can receive messages; a faint dot);
  - *active* (Joma: you are using a device; a full dot).
- **Proposal for the default:** contacts see one sum of your devices: active if any
  device is active, else reachable, else nothing.
- **Per contact, you can show your devices:** "active on laptop", "phone reachable".
  It is useful for close people and colleagues, off for everyone else.
- **Per device, you can make it invisible:** for example, a work machine never says
  you are active.
- **What cannot be hidden:** Jami's reachability per device, since contacts connect to
  each device directly. Invisible only covers what Joma sends.
- **Proposal for "online":** make it quieter. The faint dot stays, but the header says
  "can receive messages" instead of "on Jami".

- [ ] A:

# D. Accounts and agents

**Q7. Multiple accounts and multiple devices are two different things.**

- **Accounts (J8):** separate identities, like private and work. Each has its own
  contacts and devices.
- **Devices** (this discussion): the places one identity lives.
- **Proposal:** devices first (Q2–Q5), then multiple accounts. The devices page is built
  per account from the start, so J8 does not have to redo it.

- [ ] A:

**Q8. Agents (ACP) among your things.**

ACP, the Agent Client Protocol, connects a client to a coding agent: JSON-RPC, usually
over the agent's standard input and output. Joma would be the client: it runs an
agent and lets you talk to it, from any of your devices.

- **Proposal: an agent is not a linked device.** A linked device holds the account's
  keys and receives every conversation: an agent would read all your chats.
- **An agent gets its own Jami account, created by Joma on the machine where it runs**
  ("claude@zoma"). Joma marks it as yours in the "you" group of Contacts.
  - You write to it like a contact, from the laptop or the phone.
  - The Joma on that machine passes the messages to the agent through ACP and sends
    back the answers, the tool permissions to approve, and the files.
- **Permissions:**
  - an agent sees only its own conversation;
  - it acts only on its machine;
  - the tool approvals arrive as messages with buttons.
- **Later:** an agent can be shared with a contact (a colleague talks to your agent) by
  adding them to its conversation.

- [ ] A:

# E. Order

**Q9. Proposed order.**

| | What | Why |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | The delivery test (Q5) and the devices page with linking (Q2) | checks the base; linking is needed for everything else |
| D2 | Sending to your devices: files, clipboard, images (Q3) | small, daily use |
| D3 | What contacts see per device (Q6) | extends the presence already built |
| D4 | Screen between your devices, then remote control (Q4) | the share exists; the control is new and needs care |
| D5 | Agents through ACP (Q8) | builds on D1–D2 |
| J8 | Multiple accounts | after the devices, on the same pages |

- [ ] A:
